newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: ALICE TO DARWIN RAIL LINK IN HANDS OF PM
The South Australian Premier says the Alice Springs to Darwin rail link is now in the hands of the Prime Minister.
John Olsen and the Northern Territory's Chief Minister Shane Stone will meet John Howard on Thursday, in the hope of getting a A$300-million commitment to build the railway.
Mr Olsen says South Australia and the Territory have been refining a rail business plan for the past six months, and it's now time for the Federal Government to keep an 86-year-old promise.
Mr Olsen says the environmental assessment has been concluded, the rail line has now been surveyed and legislation passed both in South Australia and the Northern Territory.

"We've been pursing with the Prime Minister the need for this to receive Centenary Federation funding, that it meets the criteria of the fund that he has personaly put in place for national infrastructure," he said.
TAX DEDUCTIBLE UNIVERSITY FEES
There's a proposal to make university fees tax deductible.
It's among recommendations to be outlined at a Higher Education funding conference in Adelaide this week.
The Convenor, Jonathon Pincus, says students will have to get used to paying fees, if they want a quality education.
But Professor Pincus says under his proposal, the Government would allow students to deduct fees against future income, as far as 20 years into their careers.
And, he says comments by the Federal Education Minister, Amanda Vanstone, appear to support the proposal.

Professor Pincus says when the minister talked about the opposition to allowing universities to charge fees for students who aren't eligible for taxpayer subsidy through operating grants, she said "why should we prevent somebody from investing in their own future."
GYMPIE STRIVES TO CAPITALISE ON "HELLTOWN" TAG
The people of Gympie in southern Queensland plans to turn around the recent publicity tag of Helltown - Australia's Murder capital, with a play on words.
Cooloola mayor Mick Vernados says a meeting on Friday of community leaders ruled out legal action against the author of the Penthouse magazine article.
He says the community's decided to capitalise on the national attention with a revamped catch phrase that labels Gympie a "Hell-of-a-town".
"We've received very bad adverse publicity nationally," Mr Vernados said.

"And we're just going to turn this adversity into a positve because we want to let the people out there know what a good community Gympie and Cooloola is. It's great place in which to live, work and retire to. We're a Hell-of a-town," he said.
SURGEONS WORK TO SAVE PENIS
Microsurgeons in northern New South Wales are attempting to save a man's penis after he cut it off, at Byron Bay early this morning.
Ambulance officers say the 22-year old was at his home when the incident occurred. He was rushed to Lismore Base Hospital where he has undergone surgery.
